name: OX Quiz Widget
description: A mobile-first educational O/X quiz interface that presents one question at a time and shows answer feedback, progress, and a retry option.

requirement.summary: Build an O/X quiz widget for an educational mobile app. It shows questions one at a time, lets the user answer with O or X, reveals the correct answer with an explanation, tracks progress, and supports restarting the quiz.
details: Display the quiz question list one question at a time
Provide O and X answer buttons for the user to choose from
After an answer is selected, reveal the correct answer and show an explanation
Lock the answer buttons after a selection to prevent changing the answer, then provide a control to move to the next question
Display progress as text (e.g., '3/10 문제 완료') and as a visual progress bar
Show a completion summary with the score once all questions are answered
Provide a retry feature that resets all state and starts the quiz again from the first question

Component structure: QuizContainer (overall quiz layout), QuestionCard (current question display), AnswerButtons (O/X selection buttons), ProgressBar (progress display), ResultDisplay (correct/incorrect feedback)
State management: current question index, user answers, correctness of each answer, and quiz completion status
Accept quiz data (question text, correct answer O/X, explanation) through props, with built-in sample data for the demo
Responsive design optimized for mobile and tablet viewports
Transition animations for question changes, answer feedback reveal, and progress bar updates, implemented with Tailwind transition/animation utilities

Accessibility: full keyboard navigation (Tab focus, Enter/Space activation, optional O/X key shortcuts), visible focus indicators, ARIA labels on buttons, aria-live announcements for feedback, and progressbar role with aria-valuenow
Color scheme: green for correct answers, red for incorrect answers, gray for neutral/unselected states
Typography: use the system default font stack (Tailwind font-sans)
Styling must use Tailwind CSS utility classes only, with no custom CSS files or inline style objects
